mechanism_claims.claim_text: Synthetic Morone piscidins have source-supported antibacterial phenotypic activity with MIC/MBC endpoints against fish and human bacterial pathogens in the primary Table 3 matrix.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SB P1, WB P1, SB/WB P3, SB P4, WB P5, WB P6, and SB P7 synthetic piscidins

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Antibacterial and antiprotozoal activity of piscidins;xml:table=3

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is phenotypic activity evidence; it does not identify a molecular antibacterial target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Primary Table 4 supports antiprotozoal phenotypic activity against Tetrahymena pyriformis using PCmin and PC100 endpoints, with Class II/III piscidins showing lower PC endpoints than piscidin 1 forms.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: SB P1, WB P1, SB P4, WB P5, WB P6, and SB P7 against Tetrahymena pyriformis

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Antibacterial and antiprotozoal activity of piscidins;xml:table=4

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source tested one protozoan species; no broader protozoan range is inferred.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: For striped bass piscidin 7, the primary figure-captioned microscopy evidence supports Tetrahymena pellicle disruption after peptide exposure.
direct_assay_types: light microscopy morphology after peptide exposure
mechanism_claims.limitations: The figure supports membrane/pellicle disruption for SB P7 in Tetrahymena; it should not be generalized to all piscidins or to bacterial targets.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Table 3 provides MIC/MBC phenotypes only; bacterial killing mechanism is not promoted beyond phenotypic activity.
